card.title: Articles and prepositions — the small words that decide marks

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Articles signal known-vs-new (a/an = first mention, the = identified) and prepositions anchor time, place and relation (in/on/at, for/since, by/with). They are daily-life glue — every shop sign, notice and message depends on them — and NEB's favourite 2-mark hunting ground because the rules are small, sharp and breakable.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: a/an = one-of-many (sound decides: an honest, a university) · the = identified/unique/superlative (the sun, the first, the promises she made) · zero article: plural/general truths, meals, languages, games · time: at (point) / on (day) / in (period) · since (point) / for (duration)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Sound, not spelling, picks a/an (vowel SOUND: an hour, an honest girl; 'w/u' consonants: a university, a European). 'The' needs identifiability — previously mentioned, unique, or post-modified ('the promises she made'). Prepositions pair by collocation (good AT, married TO, different FROM), not logic.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 'She is AN honest girl' (silent h → vowel sound) and 'keeps THE promises she made' (post-modified → identified) — both NEB 2021 traps in one sentence. Superlatives and ordinals force 'the' (the best, the first). Uncountables take no a/an (advice, furniture, information — never 'an advice').

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 'She is ___ honest girl and always keeps ___ promises she ___ made': (1) AN honest (vowel sound); (2) THE promises (identified by the clause); (3) zero article before 'made' (verb, not noun) — full answer 'an / the / –' (NEB 2021, 2 marks). Three blanks, three different rules, one method: sound → identifiability → part of speech.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Collocations defeat rules ('in the morning' but 'at night'; 'on foot' but 'by bus') — memorise the pairs. Article systems differ across languages (Nepali has none), so transfer errors persist; only reading volume rewires the instinct.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Derive article choice as a decision tree: (1) uncountable/plural-general → zero; (2) singular countable → identified? the : a/an; (3) a/an → vowel sound? an : a. Prepositions derive from collocation sets, not geometry: time-scale (at<on<in), transport (by vehicle, on foot), attachment (good at, afraid of, married to).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Read the blank's noun: proper/uncountable-general → likely zero; clause after it → the; vowel sound → an. Preposition blanks: check the adjective/verb before it (good AT, different FROM, arrive AT/IN). Superlative/ordinal nearby → the.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2021 (2): article trio — 'an honest girl … the promises'. NEB 2024 (2): economic/economical + verb-choice MCQ (vocabulary bank). Preposition collocations and article error-correction rotate yearly.
